notes.summary: Finite-interval comparison identifies every genuine psh Legendre level with its P ceiling relative to the unchanged initial potential. Decreasing rays give decreasing closed levels, but no general entropy or mass continuity follows.
notes.detailedSummary: For an actual finite-energy weak ray u from w, a genuine omega-psh level chi_lambda=inf_t(u_t-lambda t) satisfies P_w[chi_lambda]=chi_lambda. The proof compares max(u_t,h+lambda t) with u_t+Ct/T on finite intervals. It assumes a genuine psh level and does not import an unchecked minimum principle. Decreasing rays from the identical start give decreasing levels, including minus-infinite limits. This concerns relative ceilings, not absolute endpoint invariance or general model approximation.
notes.text:
Fix a smooth connected compact Kahler manifold, w in E1, dd^c=i/(2pi) partial bar-partial, and t=-log|tau|^2. Let u be an actual weak ray: it is strongly continuous at zero and the canonical finite-energy geodesic on every finite interval, using the foundations retained in supplied R. Put chi_lambda=inf_{t>=0}(u_t-lambda t), and P_w[h]=(lim_{C->infinity}P_omega(h+C,w))^*.

Claim: if chi_lambda is a genuine omega-psh function, then P_w[chi_lambda]=chi_lambda. Proof: chi_lambda<=w. For C>0 and any psh competitor h<=w, h<=chi_lambda+C, the function max(u_s,h+lambda s) is a finite-energy subgeodesic on [0,T], with boundary values at most w and u_T+C. The canonical geodesic between those latter values is u_s+Cs/T. Comparison gives h+lambda t<=u_t+Ct/T. Take T to infinity, then the infimum over t. Thus h<=chi_lambda. Every rooftop P_omega(chi_lambda+C,w) equals chi_lambda, itself a competitor, proving the ceiling equality.

For actual rays u_j decreasing pointwise to an actual ray u from the identical w, inf_j inf_t=inf_t inf_j proves chi_{u_j}(lambda) decreases to chi_u(lambda) at every point and level. This includes an identically minus-infinite limit. That limit is only an extended placeholder, with P_w[-infinity]=-infinity; it is not assigned a singularity metric or probability measure.

The recognition lemma explicitly assumes a genuine psh level. All explicit levels in n2 are proved psh separately. These arguments establish neither a suitable general model sequence nor mixed-mass or entropy continuity. They do not identify the relative ceiling with the absolute smooth-background ceiling P_0. The original P19.2 remains unresolved.

The proof is retained in P19.2-paper.md and the standalone P19.2-paper.tex/P19.2-paper.pdf. Rerun python build_paper.py. This is an unverified mathematical draft.

notes.summary: An explicit construction on CP^n, n>=2, retains C’s unbounded finite-entropy start exactly. Actual relatively ample rational models recover energy, uniform radial entropy and every relative P level, including the collapsing zero boundary. This is a special case, not general P19.2.
notes.detailedSummary: On C’s hyperplane blowup use L_s=T-sE and s_j=1-1/j. The graph embedding proves relative ampleness. The usual data are -s min(v(H),1), with central multiplicities one, energy (1-(1-s)^(n+1))/(n+1)-s and entropy 1-(1-s)^n. Retaining C’s radial initial potential w, its conjugate F_w has F_w(0)=+infinity. Actual maximal rays have roof (x-(1-s))_+, and their exact relative levels are V_d with d=min(1,1-s-lambda), raw mixed masses d^k and V_{1/j} decreasing to minus infinity at zero. An integrable uniform entropy remainder proves arbitrary joint model/time convergence. The result covers one prescribed radial maximal-ray signature on projective space.
notes.text:
This new restricted construction uses supplied R and C and n1. It is an unverified draft special theorem; the entire original P19.2 is not solved.

Work on X=CP^n over C, n>=2, with FS form of volume one, dd^c=i/(2pi) partial bar-partial and t=-log|tau|^2. Let p=[1:0:...:0], H={Z_0=0}, rho=log sum_{i=1}^n|Z_i/Z_0|^2, Q_0=log(1+exp rho), delta=1/3, F(x)=x log x+(1-x)log(1-x), and C_*=2/3-F(delta). Retain exactly C’s initial potential w=Q-Q_0: Q=-(-rho)^(1/3)+C_* for rho<=-1, Q=delta rho-F(delta) until rho=-log2, and Q=Q_0 thereafter. C grants that this w is nonpositive, full mass, E1, finite probability entropy and singular only at p.

Direct conjugacy gives F_w(x)=2/(3 sqrt(3x))-C_* for 0<x<delta, and F(x) for delta<=x<=1, with F_w(0)=+infinity. Values match at delta; derivatives jump from -1 to -log2. On the inner interval F_w'=-(3x)^(-3/2) and F_w''=(2 sqrt3)^(-1)x^(-5/2).

Blow up H times {0} in X times P1, with exceptional divisor E and T=pi_X^*O(1). For rational s=A/M in (0,1), L_s=T-sE is actually relatively ample. Indeed sections Z_0,tau Z_1,...,tau Z_n have center ideal locally (Z_0,tau). Their blowup graph embeds into X times P^n times A1; divided sections give g with g^*O(1)=T-E. Thus M L_s=(M-A)T+A(T-E) pulls back O(M-A,A), relatively ample by positive projective powers and Segre. Away from zero it is the product O(M). The actual fixed factor is (Z_0,tau)^A, pulling back to O(-AE), with additional bundle factor T^(M-A).

Both central multiplicities are one. C grants T^n E=0, T^(n+1-r)E^r=-1 for 2<=r<=n+1, and relative canonical divisor E. With a=1-s, expansion gives probability masses a^n at the trivial valuation and 1-a^n at ord_H, energy e_s=(1-a^(n+1))/(n+1)-s, and entropy h_s=1-a^n. The actual model datum is eta_s(v)=-s min(v(H),1), including supported semivaluations with v(H)=+infinity. No multiplicity is discarded.

The actual singular-start ray is b_{s,t}=sup_{0<x<=1}{x rho-F_w(x)-t(x-a)_+}-Q_0. It starts at the identical w and obeys w-st<=b_{s,t}<=w. At s=1 it is Q(rho-t)-Q_0.

Here is the weak-geodesic check. Bounded radial weights Q_m=m^(-1)log(exp(mQ)+exp(m(Q_0-m))) decrease to Q. They are C1 and strictly convex, with endpoint slopes zero and one. Their conjugates increase to F_w, with F_m(0)=m. Replacing F_w by F_m gives bounded rays: on active pieces their two-variable gradients lie on (x,-(x-a)_+), so the homogeneous complex determinant vanishes. First derivatives match at interfaces; the corner produces a plateau rather than a gradient jump. Local Hessians are bounded off the axes. Bedford–Taylor products equal the almost everywhere determinant there, and bounded products do not charge p or H on finite annuli. Comparison identifies the bounded canonical geodesics. Their decrease converges to b_s by compactness of maximizing moments; a moment tending to zero is excluded by F_m>=F_N and F_N(0)=N for arbitrary N. Decreasing finite-energy continuity applies since b_s>=w-st. Every competitor below limiting boundaries is below all approximating geodesics, preserving the Perron characterization. The bound |b_{s,t}-b_{s,T}|<=s|t-T| checks strong boundary continuity. Thus these are actual weak rays.

Their usual datum comes from the actual total potential. At generic Gauss divisors rho=ht+O(1). Near p, h<=0 and the reference coefficient is zero; near H, h=v(H)>=0 and the reference coefficient is h. The leading total coefficient is sup_{0<=x<=1}(xh-(x-a)_+): use a finite lower bound on F_w for the upper estimate, and fix x>0 before taking the time limit for the lower estimate. No F_w(0) or w(p) is divided by time. Subtracting the reference coefficient gives zero near p and -s min(h,1) near H. R’s divisorial determination identifies eta_s on the full carrier.

The transported top probability is n x^(n-1)dx. Energy differentiation gives E(b_{s,t})=E(w)-t int_a^1(x-a)n x^(n-1)dx=E(w)+t e_s, first bounded and then by decreasing E1 continuity. R’s zero-defect criterion identifies b_s=r(w,eta_s), and b_1=r(w,phi) for C’s phi=-min(v(H),1). For s_j=1-1/j, datum error is exactly 1/j, energy and entropy converge, rays decrease, and ordered distance is d1(b_{s_j,t},b_{1,t})=t(e_{s_j}-e_1).

All closed levels are explicit. For d>0 define V_d=sup_{0<x<=d}(x rho-F_w(x))-Q_0. Its total weight is Q where Q'(rho)<=d and d rho-F_w(d) otherwise, with matching slopes, hence globally psh. It retains the actual w near p and has pole coefficient 1-d on H. For lambda<=0, time duality constrains (x-a)_+<=-lambda, yielding V_{min(1,a-lambda)}. For -lambda>0 strict feasibility and the derivative of the convex time objective verify duality. At lambda=0,a>0 the time limit restricts to (0,a]. At a=0 the ray tends to minus infinity everywhere, also at H where its value is -t. Positive levels are identically minus infinite. By n1 each genuine V_d equals its actual P ceiling relative to w, as a function, not merely I data.

Polarizing radial Hessians gives mixed nonpolar distribution d(Q_d'^k Q_0'^(n-k)), whose endpoint values are zero and d^k. Matching slopes exclude interface atoms; divisorial mass on H is excluded by nonpluripolarity. Hence M_k(V_d)=d^k for 1<=k<=n. The constrained d values decrease to the target. At positive d the ceilings decrease to V_d; at zero F_w(x)->+infinity proves V_{1/j} decreases to identically minus infinity. Boundary raw masses are j^(-k), and uniform profile mass errors are <=k/j. No probability or singularity metric is assigned to the minus-infinite placeholder. For genuine interior levels only, DDNL arXiv:1909.00839v1 Lemma 3.4 gives dS=(n+1)^(-1) sum_{k=1}^n(d_j^k-d^k)<=n/(2j). Its convention is matched by potential V_d/(2pi) with unchanged background, so currents and masses coincide.

Entropy has a uniform formula. Set p_w(x)=exp(F_w'(x))/(1+exp(F_w'(x))), equal to (1+exp((3x)^(-3/2)))^(-1) below delta and x above. On active pieces rho=F_w'(x)+t 1_{x>a}; plateaus and the kink have zero top mass. The FS density is x^(n-1)/(F_w''(x)p(rho)^(n-1)p'(rho)). Subtracting the initial log density gives t+(n+1)log(p_w+exp(-t)(1-p_w)) above a and zero below. Consequently H(b_{s,t})=H(w)+t h_s+(n+1)int_a^1 n x^(n-1)log(p_w+exp(-t)(1-p_w))dx. The correction lies between B_n=(n+1)int_0^1 n x^(n-1)log p_w dx and zero. B_n is finite because the tail is O(x^(n-5/2)), integrable for n>=2. This proves finite-time entropy and H(w)+B_n<=H(b_{s,t})-t h_s<=H(w), uniformly in s,t. Every joint j_l,t_l->infinity therefore has H(b_{s_{j_l},t_l})/t_l->1.

Evidence: python check_models.py passed 4,785 exact rational model cases, 4,263 profile-grid cases, 19 chain cases, 3,534 chain chart-generator checks and 10 tail cases in its recorded finite domains. Uncertified Simpson quadrature gives H(w) approximately 0.457927 and B_2 approximately -2.353133; for n=2,j=100,t=1000, H/t approximately 0.998235734 versus model slope 0.9999. These observations do not prove the analytic argument.

The complete paper is P19.2-paper.md, P19.2-paper.tex and P19.2-paper.pdf. Source applications and returned read scopes are in source-application-ledger.json and source-read-scopes.json. Rerun python check_models.py and python build_paper.py. This construction is confined to the specified radial start and hyperplane maximal-ray signature on CP^n. General compact Kahler inputs, arbitrary starts/nonmaximal rays and log-discrepancy regularization remain unresolved.

notes.summary: R gives general fixed-start maximal-model recovery, but an energy defect prevents this mechanism from recovering an arbitrary nonmaximal ray. This is a mechanism limitation, not universal nonexistence.
notes.detailedSummary: For finite-entropy w and finite NA entropy phi on a fixed smooth compact Kahler manifold, R’s strong/entropy model recovery gives rays r(w,eta_j) retaining w, bounded-time d1 convergence, and converging individual energy and entropy slopes. A common upper maximal ray bounds distance by tB_j with B_j tending to zero. For an arbitrary target ray with positive energy defect delta, the particular maximal-model mechanism has asymptotic chordal distance at least delta. General P boundaries, joint or fixed-time entropy, and other arbitrary-ray mechanisms remain unresolved.
notes.text:
Use supplied R only in its fixed smooth compact Kahler signature. Let H(w)<infinity and H_alpha(phi)<infinity, and take its actual relatively Kahler models eta_j strongly converging to phi with converging NA entropy. Define u_j=r(w,eta_j), u=r(w,phi), retaining the identical start w. Set lambda_j=max(eta_j,phi). The supporting inequality gives 0<=E_alpha(lambda_j)-E_alpha(phi)<=int|eta_j-phi| MA_alpha(phi)->0. Thus B_j=2E_alpha(lambda_j)-E_alpha(eta_j)-E_alpha(phi)->0. Order, energy affinity and ordered distance through the genuine common upper ray r(w,lambda_j) give d1(u_{j,t},u_t)<=tB_j. This proves uniform bounded-time recovery and energy-slope recovery. R gives each entropy slope H_alpha(eta_j), converging to H_alpha(phi). Convexity of entropy plus finite contracted energies, with finite initial and recession values, also gives finite entropy at finite times.

These conclusions do not establish fixed-time entropy continuity, a uniform joint limit or general closed P recovery. Round140’s stronger joint proof was checked for its normalization issue, not wholly reproved: primary MP Lemma 5.3.2 uses mean-zero slots and constant-invariant relative J, not d1 after arbitrary mean changes.

For an arbitrary nonmaximal actual ray v from w, let c_v be its energy slope and phi its usual datum. R gives delta=E_alpha(phi)-c_v>0 and d1(r(w,phi)_t,v_t)=t delta. Energy is 1-Lipschitz for d1, so liminf_{t->infinity}d1(r(w,eta_j)_t,v_t)/t >= |E_alpha(eta_j)-c_v|, tending to delta. This particular mechanism converges to maximalization rather than v. It is not a nonexistence theorem for other approximation classes, and the original arbitrary-weak-ray branch is not discarded.

Proofs are retained in section 5 of P19.2-paper.md and its standalone PDF. Source normalization records are in source-application-ledger.json; rerun python build_paper.py. General P19.2 remains unresolved.

notes.summary: The entire unchanged P19.2 remains unsolved. The toric bad sequence is an implication diagnostic, and C is an absolute-endpoint obstruction. A standalone partial paper, frozen inputs, source records and rerunnable checks were saved.
notes.detailedSummary: T verifies round140’s actual chain sequence: energy, entropy and fixed negative levels recover the trivial target, while the closed endpoint does not. A product sequence works for that target, so no nonexistence follows. The new singular-start construction is narrower than the original task. Candidate=false reflects unresolved general classes and starts, arbitrary nonmaximal rays, general boundaries, entropy requirements and log-discrepancy/cohomological regularization. Structural validation and compilation passed without mathematical certification.
notes.text:
The entire unchanged original P19.2 completion criterion is unmet; candidate=false. No original target completion is claimed.

Critical reconstruction using T: for j>=2 take positive roof weights a_i=j^(-3) for i<j and a_j=1-1/j-(j-1)j^(-3), speeds 1/i and total c_j=1-1/j. The actual regular blowup chain has vectors (1,i), central multiplicities 1,i, coefficients d_i=-sum_k a_k min(1,i/k), and rational bundle p_X^*O(1)+sum d_iF_i. Component degrees are 1-c_j and a_i/i, strictly positive. Its resolved roof-node monomial ideal has fixed divisor factor -M D_j. T therefore verifies actual relatively ample models in its precise P1 zero-start scope. Norm and entropy R_j=sum a_i/i and energy -int g_j tend to zero; -2<=H(u_{j,t})-tR_j<=0. Every fixed negative level is eventually zero, yet the endpoint is w_{c_j}, raw mass 1/j and distance c_j/2 from the trivial target’s endpoint. This is an implication failure. The product sequence works for that target, so it is no existence obstruction.

C likewise grants only its finite-entropy absolute endpoint failure. It does not prove universal approximation nonexistence or failure of singular-start-relative ceilings. The construction in n2 retains its actual singular start and recovers the collapsing relative endpoint.

Remaining indispensable gaps are simultaneous recovery of arbitrary finer P data and arbitrary E1 starts in general compact Kahler classes; general closed boundary and raw mixed-mass continuity, distinguishing genuine zero-mass levels from minus-infinite placeholders; arbitrary nonmaximal actual weak-ray mechanisms; exact log-discrepancy/cohomological regularization beyond verified polarized domains; and required fixed-time entropy or hybrid measure conclusions. The special theorem cannot close these requirements. Known polarized Fujita regimes remain established subcases.

Complete supplied bodies R/T/C and round140 were read and retained. DDNL arXiv:1909.00839v1 was pinned from primary metadata and reread at Lemma 3.4, applied only to genuine ordered interior types. DXZ arXiv:2302.02541v3 relative definitions, DZ arXiv:2509.15173v2 log-discrepancy data and complete Theorem 10.1 proof, MP’s normalized mixed estimate and MPWN’s constructive recovery proof were checked within their returned units. No full primary-PDF or recursive-proof read is claimed, and no expanded transcendental or prescribed-boundary theorem was inferred.
